article_notes: Retrospective study of 44 PCR-confirmed B. vogeli dogs at a university teaching hospital in Thailand, grouped as single B. vogeli infection (n=33) vs B. vogeli + E. canis co-infection (n=11). The groups are defined by infection status, not by severity or outcome: Tables 1 and 2 compare signalment, clinical signs and haematology/biochemistry between the infection groups. No severity grading, complication status or outcome was recorded, so no marker-severity rows can be extracted. The authors conclude that co-infection increases severity only from lower RBC, haemoglobin and haematocrit in the co-infected group; this is a marker difference between infection groups, not a test of co-infection against a severity outcome. No healthy control group.
